cards.explanation: The grace and peace come from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ. Paul says, "Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ." (2 Thessalonians 1:2) Notice where the gift comes from, friends. It isn't from Paul or his team. It comes from the Father and the Son.

The word is growing, friends! Paul says their "…faith is growing more and more…" (2 Thessalonians 1:3) Not a little. More and more. That's the kind of rising I wish my dough would do on a cold morning.
The answer is False. Paul says their "…love for one another is increasing." (2 Thessalonians 1:3) So this love isn't cooling off, it's heating up. Better than any oven in my bakery.

Paul boasts about their perseverance and faith. He says he boasts "…about your perseverance and faith in the face of all the persecution and affliction you are enduring." (2 Thessalonians 1:4) He's bragging on how they keep going, friends. I'd be the same way about my six cookie cutter kids.

They keep going in the face of persecution and affliction. Paul says they persevere "…in the face of all the persecution and affliction you are enduring." (2 Thessalonians 1:4) That word "all" matters, friends. This church wasn't having an easy time. I think that makes their perseverance even sweeter.

The answer is False. Paul says, "…you will be counted worthy of the kingdom of God, for which you are suffering." (2 Thessalonians 1:5) So the suffering doesn't say "not worthy." He tells them they will be counted worthy of the kingdom.

The answer is relief, friends. Paul says it's right "…to grant relief to you who are oppressed…" (2 Thessalonians 1:7) After all that affliction, relief is the word. I think any tired baker knows how good that sounds.

The answer is False. Paul says God will "…grant relief to you who are oppressed and to us as well." (2 Thessalonians 1:7) He puts himself and his team in that line right next to the oppressed Thessalonians. The relief isn't for them only.

The word is heaven, friends! Paul says this happens "…when the Lord Jesus is revealed from heaven with His mighty angels" (2 Thessalonians 1:7) He isn't coming from a city or a building. He's revealed from heaven.

Jesus inflicts vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel. Paul says He is "…inflicting vengeance on those who do not know God and do not obey the gospel of our Lord Jesus." (2 Thessalonians 1:8) This is a heavy part, friends, and I think it's meant to be taken seriously. The text names who it's for, so we keep to what it says.

The answer is True. Paul says Jesus comes "…to be glorified in His saints and regarded with wonder by all who have believed, including you who have believed our testimony." (2 Thessalonians 1:10) See that "including you"? The Thessalonians are right there in the crowd.

Paul prays that God will count them worthy of His calling, friends! He says, "…that our God will count you worthy of His calling…" (2 Thessalonians 1:11) The calling belongs to God, and Paul is asking God to count them worthy of it.

Paul prays that God will fulfill every good desire and work of faith. He says God "…will powerfully fulfill your every good desire and work of faith…" (2 Thessalonians 1:11) Every good desire, every work of faith. I like how big that prayer is, friends.

The word is glorified, friends! Paul says "…so that the name of our Lord Jesus will be glorified in you, and you in Him…" (2 Thessalonians 1:12) Jesus' name is glorified in them, and they are in Him. And the whole point is His name.
